claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys is primarily governed by differences among the constituent elements' diffusion energy barriers.
Diffusion-barrier differences above a critical threshold cause selective interdiffusion.
Selective interdiffusion produces pronounced grain-boundary segregation.
Selective interdiffusion produces transient local chemical ordering.
Grain-boundary segregation and transient local chemical ordering undermine overall nanoalloy stability.
The proposed initial material is a uniformly distributed, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticle ensemble with a polycrystalline grain structure.
Tuning interatomic-potential parameters in molecular-dynamics simulations can selectively modulate individual elemental diffusion barriers.
High-temperature annealing at 800–1000 °C for 0.5–2 hours will induce measurable grain-boundary segregation.
Localized chemical ordering and grain-boundary composition mediate a transition from a homogeneous phase to segregation and possible transient phase formation.
Differences in elemental diffusion barriers produce different interdiffusion rates at high temperature.
Elements with lower diffusion barriers migrate faster and accumulate at grain boundaries.
Accumulation of faster-diffusing elements at grain boundaries promotes segregation and local chemical ordering.
Segregation becomes pronounced after temperature and exposure time exceed a critical threshold.
Large artificial or intrinsic diffusion-barrier disparities will produce significant grain-boundary segregation and phase separation at high temperatures.
Balanced diffusion kinetics will preserve a more uniform chemical composition and greater structural integrity than disparate diffusion kinetics under otherwise matched conditions.
A crossover from uniformity to segregation will occur as diffusion-barrier parameters or temperature and exposure time are varied.
The prediction is limited to simulations at 70–80% of melting temperature over nanoseconds and experiments at 800–1000 °C for up to 2 hours.
Comparable segregation in balanced-barrier and unaltered-barrier samples would disfavor diffusion-barrier disparity as the governing mechanism.
